reason: Dot-like cystoliths, lenticels and nodules are small and point-like. That is exactly PATO:0001366 punctiform ('small and resembling a point').
Semi-evergreen means keeping some foliage, between evergreen and deciduous. That is the definition of PATO:0001734.

This says where the greatest width lies (base, middle, distal third), not a named shape. Unlike 'broadest' (C366, rejected), the position is given, so it can be recorded as the place along the bearer's length where the width is greatest.

Enveloping means surrounding another part on all sides. PATO:0001772 surrounding has the synonyms enclosing and wrapping. It is relational, so the enclosed part (bud, achene, ovary, fruit) goes in through docs/odp/09-relation-to-another-part.md.

label: spiniform
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's similarity to the appearance of a spine: rigid, narrow and tapering to a sharp point. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO:0991124 setaceous and FLOPO:0991200 bract-like. PATO:0001365 spiny is the quality of bearing spines; a spine-tipped apex is FLOPO:0991210.
reason: Spiniform bristles, tendrils and trichomes are themselves shaped like spines. They do not bear spines (spiny) and are not just spine-tipped, and no PATO or FLOPO term covers this.

label: obtrullate
definition: A rhomboid quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's outline being shaped like an inverted trowel: broadest above the middle, with straight sides, the longer pair converging to the base. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO:0991185 obtriangular; the inverse of trullate.
reason: A standard angular leaf and petal outline, broadest above the middle (opposite of trullate). PATO has only the general rhomboid, and FLOPO has obtriangular but not this one.

Episepalous stamens are those on the same radius as the sepals (opposite them). This is a position relative to another part of the flower, recorded with the sepals as the second term, not a unary quality.

target: new: compound of two values (clawed FLOPO:0991169 + claw long)
reason: The word combines 'clawed' (FLOPO:0991169) with the length of the claw. It should be split into the existing clawed value and a length quality of the claw, not made a term of its own.

target: comparison or relation stated without its second term
reason: 'Darkened' is darker than the normal or surrounding colour, the same as 'darker' (C242, rejected). It gives no colour without the thing it is compared with.

target: new: qualified part present (vascular bundle PO_0005020 with transverse orientation PATO_0002502)
reason: Cross-veins are transverse veins linking parallel veins, on leaves, lemmas, glumes and fruits. PO uses 'cross-vein' only as a loose synonym on several leaf-vein orders, so the statement is best recorded as veins present that are transversely oriented.
This negates FLOPO:0991154 jointed, which has articulate/articulated as synonyms. It follows unlobed (C239).
Barely visible means not clearly visible, which is PATO:0000464 inconspicuous. Same reading as 'obscure' and 'indistinct' (C174, C175).
Closely packed sori, sporangia and tubercles are crowded. PATO:0000619 is the opposite of FLOPO:0991189 distant.
'Impressed' is read as PATO:0002416 sunken (C216), so 'not impressed' is its negation.
'Fading reddish/lavender' gives the colour the flower turns to at a later stage. The colour is the quality and the late stage is the context; 'fading' alone has no value.
Same reading as 'dichotomous' (C199): repeatedly forking in two. Repeat counts ('1-13 times') go to docs/odp/03-count-of-parts.md.

target: comparison or relation stated without its second term
reason: A comparative degree of division without the part it is compared with, like 'narrower' and 'smaller' (C244, C243).
A twiner is a plant that climbs by twining round a support. The definition of FLOPO:0991108 climbing already includes twining.

label: proliferous
definition: A structural quality inhering in a plant structure by virtue of its producing new shoots, buds, plantlets or like organs from a part that does not normally produce them. NOTE: Botany-specific; PATO:0002102 proliferative is a cellular quality (cell division).
reason: Proliferating inflorescences, fruits and fronds (with buds or plantlets) are a known botanical character. The only PATO term, proliferative, is about cells dividing.
Prickled means bearing prickles, and PO has the part (PO:0025169, an outgrowth of the epidermis). Same as lenticellate (C204). This is more exact than the earlier 'aculeate' → spiny rule (C307).
Dish-shaped hypanthia, disks and stigmas are round and shallowly concave, which is the definition of FLOPO:0991182 saucer-shaped.
The same words in the other order: covered with stalked glands.

label: tubercle-based
definition: A shape quality inhering in a trichome by virtue of the trichome's arising from an enlarged, wart-like multicellular base. NOTE: When a stem or leaf is said to have tubercle-based hairs, the quality inheres in the trichome (PO:0000282), recorded as a part of the stated bearer.
reason: A common and diagnostic hair type (grasses, Boraginaceae). FLOPO:0991060 tuberculate describes a surface with tubercles, not a hair's base.
Awn-like tips and calyx lobes are very narrow, stiff and bristle-like, which is what setaceous means. A real awn present would be the aristate rule (C207).
Declined pedicels, flowers, stamens and styles point obliquely downward, which is FLOPO:0991207 descending.
Not exserted means not sticking out beyond the enclosing part, which is the positive term FLOPO:0991121 included (opposite of PATO:0000623 exserted).
PATO:0001368 erose (irregularly toothed edge) lists jagged as a RELATED synonym. All the examples are margins or teeth.

label: cone-like
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's architecture resembling a cone (strobilus): a compact, ovoid to cylindrical structure of densely overlapping scales or bracts on a short axis. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO:0991142 spike-like; not PATO:0002021 conical, which is a geometric cone shape.
reason: Cone-like catkins, spikes and fruiting spadices look like a strobilus, not a geometric cone. This matches the earlier '-like' architecture terms.
Beaded rhizomes, filaments and fruits are narrowed at regular intervals. That is FLOPO:0991168 moniliform (synonym bead-like, with torulose as a related synonym).
Negation of PATO:0001979 lobed, the same as unlobed (C239).
